identity.result: the same object as the lensed supernova 'SN Athena' (named by another team), discovered in October 2025 with JWST/NIRCam
evidence: JWST GO 4568 (PI Pierel) target 'athena' at 64.3964033, -11.90704: 0.014 arcsec from h002

JWST DD 12781 (PI Pascale, Cycle 5, 9.7 h, status Implementation) abstract: 'The strongly lensed SN Athena was discovered in October 2025 with JWST/NIRCam by comparing new observations with archival 2022 imaging of the z=0.87 “question mark” galaxy, which is quintuply imaged by the foreground cluster MACS J0417'
no refereed paper or arXiv preprint on SN Athena found (literature subagent, 2026-10-18)
identity.consequence: not a first discovery by this project; its type is to be confirmed by that team's NIRSpec PRISM spectrum

other_team_prediction: 12781 abstract: three new lens models 'conservatively predict that Athena will reappear between mid-August 2026 and early March 2027 in a counterimage only a few arcseconds away'
this_project_prediction: single public glafic v3 model (#309): counter-image ~7.6 arcsec away lags 708-778 d (sample range of 10 realisations; best fit 748 d) -> 2027-09-14 to 2027-11-22; position 0.8-1.1 arcsec from catalogued 1c.2; model-to-model uncertainty not covered

depth_estimate: estimate, not an ETC result: the expected counter-image signal (~200-330 nJy F150W, #308) against forced-photometry errors of 4.5 nJy (1208) and 12.2 nJy (VENUS, 1,245 s) in the 0.15 arcsec aperture gives S/N ~16-73 for a single VENUS- or 1208-like visit; depth is not the limiting factor
